intro: From the moment you quit smoking, your body starts to repair itself. The timeline below is based on the World Health Organization's list.
note: Source: WHO · Varies from person to person.

items.label: 20 minutes
items.text: Your heart rate and blood pressure drop.

items.label: 12 hours
items.text: The carbon monoxide level in your blood returns to normal.

items.label: 2–12 weeks
items.text: Your circulation improves and your lung function increases.

items.label: 1–9 months
items.text: Coughing and shortness of breath decrease.

items.label: 1 year
items.text: Your risk of coronary heart disease falls to about half that of a smoker.

items.label: 5–15 years
items.text: Your risk of stroke falls to that of someone who has never smoked.

items.label: 10 years
items.text: Your risk of lung cancer falls to about half that of a smoker. The risks of cancer of the mouth, throat, oesophagus, bladder, cervix and pancreas also decrease.

items.label: 15 years
items.text: Your risk of coronary heart disease becomes that of someone who has never smoked.
